solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having started under a misapprehension

definitions.meaning: a runner or batsman who has got going is said to be ...
being wide of the target, mistaken or wrong

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom has two senses: having begun scoring or running, and being inaccurate or mistaken.

clue.text: Priest swallows drug — it helps during flight

indicators.note: the priest's title takes the drug into its middle, as if gulping it down

parts.note: a Catholic priest is addressed as Father
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes drugs, and something helps him through a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a nervous air passenger; the definition really describes a bird's plume.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumes on a bird's wing give it lift and control in the air, so a quill aids flying.

clue.text: Anita Stewart shows discrimination

indicators.note: the name displays a run of letters across its two parts, so it shows the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A woman named Anita Stewart is discerning in her judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement in matters of style or quality is called discernment, a synonym for discrimination.

clue.text: Old Italian banker certain of being unmasked

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
a river has banks, so a banker is a river; the Po flows through northern Italy
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A former Italian financier is sure to be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword shorthand for a river, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being revealed or laid bare to public view is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Finished article on location in disarray

parts.note: something finished is all over
the is the definite article
a place is a location

explanation.surface: A completed newspaper piece about a venue is a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered or chaotic, a synonym for disordered.

clue.text: Arouse and race the French

parts.note: a kind is a sort or race, as in humankind
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Stir things up and compete against the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle feelings is to stir them up or excite them, a synonym.

clue.text: Mark gets superb staff

parts.note: ace means excellent or superb

explanation.surface: A marker receives an excellent rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial club or rod carried as a symbol of office is a kind of staff.

clue.text: Search through bog in North Africa

indicators.note: the search goes through the middle of the bog, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a marsh is a bog
to rake is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone searches through a swamp somewhere in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan city is located in the north-west of Africa, so the definition is a location description.

clue.text: Mere cop arranged to host show

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, which is what arranging does

explanation.surface: A mere policeman is set up to present a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as master of ceremonies at an entertainment is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Flower cut for the platform

indicators.note: the flower is shortened by having its final letter removed

parts.note: a daisy is a flower

explanation.surface: A flower is cut for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised floor at one end of a hall is a dais, a kind of platform.

clue.text: Random pile scattered by rotavator, for example

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about and rearranged as if strewn

explanation.surface: A rotavator scatters a random heap of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening surface misleads: 'rotavator' is cited for reading the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word rotavator reads identically in both directions, making it an example of such a word.

clue.text: Car commonly first in wish lists

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a ship lists or heels when it leans over

explanation.surface: A car is usually at the top of wish lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a car is called one's wheels, informal slang for transport.

clue.text: Convict beset by even more corrupt inhabitant

indicators.note: the convict is surrounded by the other word, which besets it

parts.note: viler means more vile or more corrupt
an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner is surrounded by someone even more corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller in a small rural settlement is an inhabitant of it.

clue.text: Solicitor for doctor

parts.note: pro means in favour of, or for
a doctor is one who cures, a curer

explanation.surface: A lawyer represents a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it means one who solicits, a pimp.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimp solicits clients for prostitutes, so is a solicitor in that sense.

clue.text: Strove to capture sovereign to be executed

indicators.note: the striving word takes the sovereign prisoner within it

parts.note: to strive against others is to compete
a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L from libra

explanation.surface: Someone strove to seize a monarch who would then be put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold pound coin; L is the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Executed in the sense of carried out or finished, a synonym.

clue.text: Needlewoman lost top for jug

indicators.note: in a down-ward sense the head letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a needlewoman is one who sews, a sewer

explanation.surface: A seamstress has lost the lid of her jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pitcher with a wide mouth is a type of jug.

clue.text: Outsider is badly grounded

indicators.note: the letters are put together poorly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outsider is poorly educated in basics.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor not expected to win is an outsider, a synonym.

clue.text: A crazy retiring architect

indicators.note: the word goes back on itself, withdrawing in the opposite direction

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A mad, shy designer of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam designed many neoclassical buildings in Britain, an example of an architect.

clue.text: Expel director and spirit abroad

parts.note: rum is a spirit
out means away, as abroad

explanation.surface: Throw out the director and his foreign drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone in disgrace is an idiom originally from military discharge.

clue.text: Follower is masterful type embracing new church

indicators.note: the masterful figure wraps its arms around the other letters

parts.note: a he-man is a dominant, macho type

explanation.surface: A disciple is a dominant figure hugging a new church.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal supporter or hired helper is a synonym for follower.

clue.text: Woman in advancing years becomes mean

indicators.note: the woman sits inside the years

parts.note: age is advancing years
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman growing older becomes unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean in statistics is an average, a synonym.

clue.text: Calm when having drinks in A&E

indicators.note: the drinks are placed inside the letters A and E

parts.note: A&E stands as two letters, A and E
teas are drinks

explanation.surface: Calm when you have drinks in a hospital emergency unit.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and untroubled is the idiomatic meaning, a synonym for calm.

clue.text: Period abroad is a complete break

definitions.meaning: Americans say period for the punctuation mark Britons name otherwise
a total halt or cessation of activity

explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation dot is called a period in America, and the phrase also means a total stop.

clue.text: Cheers original artist

indicators.note: inventive or novel, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to an innovative painter.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist known for impossible structures, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Girl caught West Indian batsman

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Brian Lara is a famous batsman from Trinidad

explanation.surface: A girl took a catch off a West Indian batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Lara is a Trinidadian cricketer, one of the West Indies' greatest batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a girl's name, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Rob and can't exchange the hot property

indicators.note: the letters swap places with one another, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thieves who rob and cannot swap the stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggled goods are illegal, and hot means stolen or illicit, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: A service return that's out of reach

indicators.note: the service's letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis service return that cannot be reached.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis surface misleads: 'service' means an armed force.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away or at a distance means unreachable, a synonym.

clue.text: Boss of breeding establishment

definitions.meaning: a knob or raised ornament, as on a shield
a farm where horses are bred

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a raised knob and a farm for breeding horses.

clue.text: Boy found in eastern borders of US national park

indicators.note: the boy is located inside the borders

parts.note: verges are borders or edges
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is discovered at the eastern edges of an American park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida wetland reserve is a national park in the United States, an example.
